prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, from bifunctional PROTAC degraders to the cereblon-dependent mechanism of molecular glues

statement.case_for: I keep B023 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The shared core of the committee's case is that a designed small molecule brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase so that the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome system destroys it, converting occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven degradation. The mechanism is chemically explicit (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker and ligase-ligand design, the cereblon degron), and independent groups have reproduced it for two decades. Handa's identification of cereblon is what links the PROTAC concept to thalidomide-type glues that are already approved drugs in patients, so the glue half has clinical validation even though no bifunctional degrader is yet approved. I judge that this makes the induced-proximity principle validated, and the remaining clinical question concerns one modality's payoff, not whether the chemistry holds. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs, and Handa gives the mechanistic discovery on the other strand. That is a coherent single achievement within three names.
statement.case_against: The attribution cost is real and I do not want to hide it. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim all have strong claims, and any three-person set leaves one strand looking under-credited. Sakamoto's part in the first PROTAC paper is only covered indirectly by crediting Crews and Deshaies. No bifunctional degrader is approved, so part of the case still looks forward, and Somfai and Zou are right that a conservative committee could wait. The combined citation also joins two strands with different histories, and if the committee decides they are two discoveries, one citation will read as artificial. Finally, B002 is more mature and more cleanly attributed, and I accept that this is a legitimate reason to prefer it, though I do not share it.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps Ciulli as the third name, arguing that VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs a general platform, and treats cereblon as target identification for one drug class. He says he would not object strongly to Handa.
responses.response: After rereading, I still choose Handa, and I will state the criterion the chair asked for: the third name should go to the independent mechanistic discovery that explains a whole class of working drugs, and not to the refinement of an existing concept. Ciulli's structure-guided work is real chemistry, but it builds on the Crews and Deshaies concept, while cereblon explains why thalidomide-type drugs act and opened the glue strand. I take your point that Ciulli is the stronger platform argument. If the committee narrows the citation to PROTACs only, I would accept Ciulli, and as you note, you would accept Handa, so our disagreement does not threaten the B023 prize itself.

responses.point: Somfai holds B002 first as overdue and cleanly attributed, and says Kosugi's tin-amide precursor is not answered by a two-name citation. He also asks whether PROTACs and glues could be split with at most three people.
responses.response: I have thought about your questions and I have not moved. I do not support a two-part split: with three names it would leave one person on one part and credit neither strand adequately, and Aqvist and Sparr call it artificial for good reason. On timing, I read the approved thalidomide-class drugs as clinical validation of the principle, and the PROTAC pipeline as an extension and not a precondition. Your overdue argument for B002 is serious, and Buchwald and Hartwig are the cleaner attribution. My difference is that I weigh a new modality over a late recognition of an extension of 2010 work. I keep B002 as my first alternative and could vote for it if B023 cannot reach a majority.

responses.point: Chabes argues that the approved thalidomide-class drugs validate the glue half, and that Handa's cereblon result makes the glue strand a mechanistic discovery and not just medicinal chemistry. He also raises a possible split into separate PROTAC and glue parts.
responses.response: I agree with the validation argument and it is the main reason I weigh the lack of an approved PROTAC less heavily than Somfai does. I differ on the split. A PROTAC part and a glue part would force a one-and-two allocation among Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and it would suggest the strands have separate histories when the common ubiquitin-ligase logic is the point. A single citation that names both PROTACs and the cereblon mechanism is more accurate, since Crews and Deshaies conceived induced degradation and Handa explained the mechanism of the glues. I would support a citation worded as yours is, with cereblon explicit.

responses.point: Zou keeps B002 first because both its discovery and its credit are settled, while conceding that B023 is conceptually fresher and that novelty may be underweighted.
responses.response: I accept that framing: B002 is the candidate whose discovery and credit are settled, and B023 is the one where the science is settled but the credit is contested. Where we differ is on which uncertainty the committee should tolerate. A prize that omits Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim carries a real attribution cost, and I do not treat that lightly. I still consider it more tolerable than recognising a second chapter of palladium cross-coupling, for which the 2010 prize already supplies a strong precedent. I would value knowing whether you could move to B023 with a configuration that credits cereblon explicitly.

uncertainties: Whether the committee settles on Handa or Ciulli as the third laureate, which decides whether the cereblon mechanism is credited in the citation.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one discovery or two; I treat them as one, but a majority could reasonably disagree.
I have not verified the current clinical status of bifunctional degraders and rely on the committee's statements that none is approved.
Whether Somfai and Zou will move off B002 under any B023 configuration, which affects whether a majority forms.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. My work on peptides, nanoparticle biosensing and biomaterials at Linkoping is adjacent to but does not overlap with B023, B002 or B021. I have no documented connection to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Buchwald or Hartwig. My postdoc mentors, Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey, are not shortlisted names. Sparr's note of overlap with me on self-assembly and membranes does not bear on B023, and I do not regard it as recusal-level.
